steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Prose literature exams typically test three skills: translation (accurate rendering of the Latin), analysis (identifying language and style features), and evaluation (discussing themes, context, and the author's purpose). | Key Fact: Translation questions require precise, idiomatic English that captures the exact meaning of the Latin. Avoid over-literal or over-free translations. | Key Fact: For analysis questions, name the stylistic feature, quote the Latin, and explain the effect: 'Caesar uses tricolon (lines 4-5) to build a sense of overwhelming force'. | Key Fact: Evaluation questions (8-10 marks) require a structured argument with introduction, multiple points supported by textual evidence, and a conclusion.
